text:
sam: quick heads-up — vendor asked us to accept a preemptible-heavy commit in exchange for a bigger discount. need clarity on how preemption credits / billing offsets actually apply to committed hours.

anita: ugh. did they spell out the credit mechanism? like do they refund $ or apply extra reserved hours back to the commit? :thinking:

li: they sent a one-pager. high level says: "preemption credits will be issued as invoice line items against future bills" — but no math. we should get examples.

sam: exact ask: 1) can we get a guaranteed non-preemptible floor for X% of committed GPUs? 2) if preemption happens, is there an automatic hour credit vs a dollar credit? 3) can credits be applied to committed utilization rather than future invoices only?

ezra: i'd push for SKU-level carveouts. our latency-critical inference pools cannot tolerate preemptible at all. ask for a carveout or explicit replacement capacity within region within N hrs.

anita: +1. Also push for a quarterly reconciliation statement that shows committed hours vs preempted hours and the resulting credit calculation. ask for a sample reconciliation table.

li: example numbers we should prepare for negotiation: assume 100 reserved A100s. vendor proposes 30% preemptible in exchange for 25% discount. what's our break-even if preemptions lead to lost availability?

sam: rough back-of-envelope: if preemptible swap causes >10% extra use of on-demand or burst pool at 2x cost, the discount disappears. need explicit fallback pricing and guaranteed replacement window.

engops-bot: invoice-snippet detected: ```
SKU: A100-EDP-RESERVE
Committed-hours: 72000
Applied-credits: 0
Preemption-events: 14

Note: line items currently do not show per-event credit math.
```

ezra: that bot snippet is perfect to send them — ask them to fill in per-event credit calc. also request SLA credits if replacement > 4 hrs.

anita: legal should review the EDP draft — specifically section on "capacity guarantees" and "credits and offsets". want to avoid credits that are only redeemable as marketing coupons or future-only non-cash credits.

li: vendor call scheduled tomorrow 10am PT. agenda suggestion: 1) define replacement SLA (hours), 2) credit math examples (per-event and monthly reconciliations), 3) non-preemptible carveouts & SKU carveouts, 4) billing treatment (cash refund vs residual commit).

sam: perfect. i'll own the agenda and ask for sample spreadsheets ahead of the call. @anita @ezra @li pls add any redlines you want legal to prep before the meeting. :thumbsup:

anita: will drop a short doc with proposed redlines in #vendors after lunch.

ezra: i'll map our critical workloads and the minimum non-preemptible floor we need.

sam: thanks all — objective: avoid an EDP that reduces effective usable reserved capacity. if they can't give concrete credit math, we ask to convert portion to dedicated (non-preemptible) at a modestly higher price.

engops-bot: action: calendar invite created for 1758324567 (vendor-edp-call). attendees: sam, anita, li, ezra.

li: bringing cost model worksheet to the call. see you all tomorrow.
